scope: D3D8 standalone RT/depth construction promotes the cached level view to an independent public count of one and transfers the original private texture device pin to that surface without adding a second pin. The existing private_back_buffer flag also marks standalone private storage. Public references beyond the first do not retain more storage or device pins. Public zero returns one storage/device pin, leaving color binding texture references and private depth-binding storage references alive. Cached GetSurfaceLevel/GetRenderTarget/GetDepthStencilSurface recovers the same view and exactly one public device pin. Additional chains transfer the promoted surface pin/storage reference as their existing chain base; ordinary texture/cube/implicit/chain models remain intact. Final device cleanup has a temporary self pin for bound-only storage callbacks. Native tests execute real public/storage/device/private-data methods with abstract color/depth storage holds; retained 39-case render-target entry tests and real XP exercise the full setter/getter path. XP renders two single-sample public-zero Clear/CopyRects/Present frames, plus verifies a four-sample RT/depth pair only for binding counters and finalization. This phase does not claim new four-sample standalone pixel coverage. Five finalizers validate proxy safety counts, not native HAL destruction counts. General root-device state preservation with external resources, complete reentrant ownership graphs, other resource public/internal counts, formats/MSAA/refresh/fullscreen/multiple buffers/Reset/thread/device-loss, original Microsoft HAL, games/FPS and review stages 4/5/6 remain incomplete. No host/protocol/shader/bundle change.

sources.evidence: Pinned Windows resource tests show standalone surfaces start at one public reference and retain one device reference; texture levels share parent counts. This is supporting creation/containment context, not a new original-HAL binding run.

Standalone public AddRef/Release uses its own resource count, retains internal texture/view storage and changes the parent device pin only on zero/nonzero edges; ordinary texture-level surfaces forward to their parent.
Standalone target construction assigns a separate parent_device. SetRenderTarget acquires internal views/storage without taking public surface references; getters return public surface references.
